What is the geographic scope of reforest.content:
First, due to long-term farming, ecological structure of most project sites is relatively homogenous, 
with low biodiversity.
The other small part is wasteland, mainly covered with grass and scattered 
shrubs.
Afforestation of this project will use local species as much as possible, implement 
afforestation activity with scientific and reasonable configuration method, with no burning and 
slash.
The use of point-like site preparation will protect the existing vegetation as much as 
possible.

Change in Biodiversity: Justification of Change | Species of plant: The  project  implemented  afforestation  activity  through  scientific  and reasonable configuration method with no burning and slash  by  planting  local  tree  species  Picea  crassifolia,  Sabina  przewalskii,  Pinus  tabulaeformis,  Populus,  Betula  and  Ulmus.  Five species of them grew up successfully expect Ulmus which  didn’t survive well due to the high altitude environment. In addition, according to field survey, there are many bushes  and grasses growing around the planted trees which has  significantly increased the species of plant in the project area.

As a result, the project has established an 
artificial forest with five native species of trees which have proved their adaptability being planted 
in high altitude area and the increased forest cover of local area could benefit local environment by 
improving the condition of local micro climate (increasing precipitation, decreasing dust weather 
and adjusting humidity, etc.).
Furthermore, the project aimed to contribute community benefits for

environment through growing of the trees, enhance the capabilities of local communities and 
residents by providing their relevant technical skills and training, and increase local biodiversity as 
a result of establishing a forest of native trees (Picea crassifolia, Sabina przewalskii, Pinus 
tabulaeformis, Populus, Betula and Ulmus).
The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 49,998,229  tCO2e in 100 years, 
with an average annual GHG emission removal of 499,982  tCO2e.
